lines.vo: Ever wake up one minute before your alarm?
That's not luck. That's your brain.
Kev pulls on his Talk Less tee, sets his alarm for six thirty, and crashes.
lines.cap: Kev pulls on his Talk Less tee, sets his alarm for 6:30, and crashes.

lines.vo: Here's what's going on inside his head.
Deep in his brain sits a master clock, about twenty thousand cells, keeping time all night.
lines.cap: Deep in his brain sits a master clock, about 20,000 cells, keeping time all night.

lines.vo: Before he wakes, his body starts releasing wake-up hormones, lifting him out of deep sleep.
In one sleep study, people told they'd be woken early had those hormones rise about an hour before.
lines.cap: In one sleep study, people told they'd be woken early had those hormones rise about an hour before.

lines.vo: So the alarm isn't waking Kev up. His brain got there first.
